meta.name: Grand Theft After-Dark
meta.sub: Real props. Real stakes. Real chaos.
meta.legal: Independent fan tribute event. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Rockstar Games, Take-Two Interactive, or any related entity.

vocabulary.handler: TJ — the star and host of the night: the cinematic Handler on the mic, the game master on the decks
vocabulary.transmission: TJ's cinematic Handler drop — read on mic / play VO
vocabulary.scene: the 4th-wall beat that turns the story into the game: TJ steps out of the fiction, names the real room, then hands the crew the rules

crewCard.madeSub: Welcome to the crew. Don't get busted.

chapters.job: The crew gets made. First contact with the Handler.
chapters.endsOn: The Handler reveals there’s a job worth eight figures.
chapters.transmission:
Listen up. I’m only saying this once.
You weren’t supposed to make it this far. Most people get made at the door. You didn’t. That tells me you’ve got something.
Name’s the Handler. I run this crew — and as of tonight, that’s you. There’s a job coming, the kind people spend their whole lives waiting for. Eight figures. One window.
But first you prove you can hang. You follow my lead, you make it out. Maybe.
Welcome to Grand Theft After-Dark. Don’t get wasted. Don’t get busted. And the only voice you trust in this room — is mine.
Now — decks are hot. Let’s play.

chapters.job: Prove you belong. The crew is tested on a small score.
chapters.endsOn: One of the crew is secretly working for someone else.
chapters.transmission:
Eight figures. That number’s been sitting in your chest since last night — I can see it on you.
Here’s the thing about a number that big: I don’t hand it to strangers. Tonight you earn the rest of it.
Small score. Low risk, high noise. All I’m doing tonight is watching — who steps up, who hides at the back, who I’d want next to me when it’s real.
And one more thing before we start. Somebody in this room isn’t only working for me. I don’t know who yet. I will.
Decks are hot. Let’s play.

chapters.job: Recruiting the getaway driver. A high-speed night.
chapters.endsOn: The driver knows a route nobody else does — to a vault.
chapters.transmission:
Nobody’s confessed yet. That’s fine — rats get tired before I do.
Tonight we don’t talk about it. Tonight we need a driver.
A score like ours lives or dies on ninety seconds of road, so I want the fastest thing in this room on my side of the car. Show me you can move.
And if the right one’s in here, they’ll know a road nobody put on a map. That road ends at a vault.
Decks are hot. Let’s drive.

chapters.job: Meeting the money launderer. Cleaning the first take.
chapters.endsOn: The Fence demands a bigger cut — or he talks.
chapters.transmission:
There’s a vault at the end of that road. Sit with that for a second.
Now the boring truth: money you can’t spend isn’t money, it’s evidence. So tonight we meet the man who makes it clean.
He’s not crew and he’s not a friend. He’s a price — and this room is going to help me pay it.
Fair warning. Men like him always come back wanting a bigger number, and they always say the same thing when they don’t get it.
Decks are hot. Let’s play.

chapters.job: Gearing up. The crew gets the hardware for what’s coming.
chapters.endsOn: The hardware came from a rival crew. They want it back.
chapters.transmission:
He asked for more. He’s going to get an answer he doesn’t like. That’s tomorrow’s problem.
Tonight we gear up. Everything this crew needs for the big one comes through that door in a case.
Hold it, get comfortable with it, make it boring — because the night we actually use it, there’s no time left to learn.
One thing, though. Hardware this good never comes clean. Somewhere in this city, somebody is about to notice theirs is missing.
Decks are hot. Let’s play.

chapters.job: Recruiting the tech. Cracking the target’s security.
chapters.endsOn: The security system belongs to the city’s biggest boss.
chapters.transmission:
A rival crew came asking about our hardware tonight. I told them to get in line.
Muscle was the easy part. What I need now is a brain — somebody who can talk to a building.
Every door on this job is electric, and electric doesn’t care how tough you are. Find me the one in here who can make a system say yes.
And when we crack it open, we’ll see whose name is on it. You’re not going to like whose name is on it.
Decks are hot. Let’s play.

chapters.job: Planting someone inside the target. Trust nobody.
chapters.endsOn: The inside man goes dark. Flipped — or dead?
chapters.transmission:
The biggest boss in this city owns the doors we’re walking through. Good. Means the take is real.
You can’t case a place like that from the street. So tonight we put one of our own on the inside.
That’s the hardest thing I will ever ask anybody in this crew to do. Whoever takes it walks in alone, smiles at people who’d bury them, and waits for my call.
In there, trust nobody. In here, trust the crew. And trust me.
Decks are hot. Let’s play.

chapters.job: The full team assembles. Last night of Act I.
chapters.endsOn: The Handler names the target: The Diamond Casino.
chapters.transmission:
Our inside man went quiet three days ago. No call, no signal, nothing.
I’m not going to stand up here and tell you he’s fine. I’m telling you we go anyway.
Look around this room. Every seat filled, every one of you earned the chair you’re in — this is the crew I ride with all the way.
After tonight there are no more small scores. Only the big one. And it has a name: the Diamond Casino.
Decks are hot. Let’s play.

chapters.job: Scouting the target. Memorizing the layout.
chapters.endsOn: Cameras catch one of the crew. The clock starts.
chapters.transmission:
The Diamond Casino. Say it once tonight, then never out loud again.
We’re going to go look at it. Not touch it — look at it. Every camera, every exit, every guard who checks his watch too often.
I want that building living in your head so well you could walk it blind. That’s the whole job: see everything, take nothing.
Careful, though. A room like that looks back.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: The plan comes together. Roles assigned.
chapters.endsOn: There are two ways in. The crew splits on which.
chapters.transmission:
A camera got one of us last night. So the clock we didn’t have yesterday is running now.
Which means tonight it stops being a dream and becomes a plan. Roles, positions, timings — everybody walks out of here knowing exactly what they are.
No passengers on this one. If you don’t know your job by last call, you’re not on it.
There are two ways into that building. I know which one I like. Tonight I want to hear which one you like.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: Rehearsing the job. Everything that can go wrong, does.
chapters.endsOn: A rehearsal goes loud. Cops are now watching.
chapters.transmission:
Half this room wants the front door. Half wants the roof. Tonight the job decides for us.
We run the whole thing. Start to finish, full speed, no shortcuts — and I want it to go wrong in here, where going wrong is free.
Every mistake you make tonight is one you don’t make in that vault. So make them early and make them loud.
Just understand what loud does. It carries. And this city has very good ears.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: Police pressure builds. The crew lays low — but parties harder.
chapters.endsOn: A detective is one step behind. He has a name: yours.
chapters.transmission:
We got heard. There are cars on this block that weren’t on it last week, and nobody in them is here to party.
So let me show you how a real crew lays low: we don’t hide. We get louder. Nobody watches the room that’s obviously having a good time.
Act like you’ve got nothing to hide and you’ll have nothing to hide. That’s the job tonight, top to bottom.
One of them is closer than the others, though. He stopped chasing the crew — he’s chasing a name now. The name he’s got is yours.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: Someone’s talking. The crew hunts the informant.
chapters.endsOn: The rat is revealed — someone the crew trusted.
chapters.transmission:
Cops don’t pull a name out of thin air. Somebody in this crew handed it to them.
I told you on night two that one of us was working two sides. Tonight we find out who.
Nobody leaves, nobody’s above it, and I don’t want a mob — I want the truth. This room happens to be very good at getting the truth.
Brace up for it. It’s going to be somebody we let all the way in.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: Calling in a debt. The crew needs a powerful ally.
chapters.endsOn: The ally agrees — now the crew owes the worst people in the city.
chapters.transmission:
We found our rat. I’m not saying the name from up here. They know, and so do you.
That cost us a body and it cost us time, so tonight I go do something I hate. I go ask for help.
I’ve got exactly one favor left in this city and I’ve been saving it for a night this bad. I’m burning it on you.
When it gets granted we’ll owe the kind of people you never want to owe. Worth it.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: Last chance to walk away. Nobody does.
chapters.endsOn: The Handler sets the date: tomorrow night, the score goes down.
chapters.transmission:
We’re in debt to the worst people in this city, and there’s only one way left to pay them. Through that vault.
Which makes tonight the last honest night any of us get. So here’s one clean way out: door’s right there. No questions, no hard feelings, no story about you afterward.
I’ll wait. I’ve done this long enough to know how this goes.
Nobody moved. Then hear the date, because it isn’t “someday” anymore. It’s tomorrow night.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: The night before the big one. Nerves, loyalty, last words.
chapters.endsOn: Lights out. Next time the doors open — it’s go time.
chapters.transmission:
Tomorrow. That’s the whole briefing. That’s the only word that matters.
So tonight isn’t about the job. Tonight is about the people who are going to do it with you.
Find whoever you’d want standing next to you in that vault and tell them so. Say the thing you’d regret not saying. Then we get loud and forget the clock for a few hours.
When the lights go down tonight, that’s the last easy breath we take. Next time those doors open, it’s go time.
Decks are hot. Let’s make tonight count.

chapters.job: THE BIG ONE. The vault. The whole night is the heist.
chapters.endsOn: The take is bigger than anyone imagined. So is the heat.
chapters.transmission:
This is it. No more rehearsals. No more talking.
Everything — every night, every favor, every body — it all led here. The vault’s open. The crew’s in position. The clock is running.
You know your jobs. You know the risks. There’s no walking out of this room the same way you walked in.
Tonight we take the whole thing. Tonight we become legends or we go down trying.
Decks are hot. Crew — let’s go to work.

chapters.job: Five stars. Choppers up. The whole city is chasing the crew.
chapters.endsOn: The crew scatters. The money’s split. Trust is gone.
chapters.transmission:
We got it. All of it. More than the plan said was in there.
And now every siren in this city is pointed at this room. Five stars. Choppers up. A badge on every bridge.
So we do the only thing left to do — we move, and we don’t stop moving. Fast, loud, together. You slow down tonight, you get taken.
Get through this one and the money is real. Get through this one and we scatter.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: Dividing the take. Greed sets in. Old grudges surface.
chapters.endsOn: Someone took more than their share. Blood is owed.
chapters.transmission:
We made it out. Barely, and not all of us in one piece.
Now the part nobody plans for. The money’s on the table and it has to be cut.
I’ve watched more crews die over a split than over a score, so we do this one in the open, in this room, in front of each other. No side deals, no quiet envelopes.
Count it twice. Because if a number comes up short tonight, somebody answers for it in blood.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: Betrayal. The crew turns on itself.
chapters.endsOn: A traitor tips off the cops — but the Handler won’t leave anyone behind.
chapters.transmission:
The count came up short, and now this crew is looking at itself sideways.
It gets worse. Whoever took it made a phone call. The cops know where we sleep.
So let me say the thing I said on night one, because nothing about it has changed: you want to know who to trust in this room, it’s me.
Get loud, stay tight, and hold each other down. Nobody in my crew gets left behind tonight — not even the one who did this.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: The Handler levels with the crew: this was never about the money.
chapters.endsOn: The truth’s out — and the crew’s tighter than it’s ever been.
chapters.transmission:
You want the truth? Fine. You’ve earned it.
Every night, every job, every favor — people kept asking me what the real score was. Here it is: it was never about the money.
I’ve run rooms for twenty-five years. Different cities. Different crews. And I’ve been waiting a long time for one like this.
The score was you. Building something that doesn’t fall apart when the lights come up — that’s the only thing I ever cared about.
So before this all comes to a head — decks are hot. Let me give you a night you’ll never forget.

chapters.job: Scores get settled. The crew and the Handler go after the ones who came for them.
chapters.endsOn: One last job remains. The biggest yet.
chapters.transmission:
I told you the truth last night and this room got tighter, not looser. That tells me everything I needed to know.
So now we settle up. The rival crew. The fence. The badge who wanted your name. Everybody who took a shot at this crew hears from us tonight.
I’m not asking anyone to be brave. I’m asking you to be loud, and together, and completely unbothered — which has always been the scariest thing in this city.
When the board’s clean, there’s still one job left on it. The biggest one yet.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: One final score. Everything on the line.
chapters.endsOn: The crew pulls it off — or goes down swinging. It ends tomorrow.
chapters.transmission:
One job left. Everything this crew has, on the table, one more time.
No favors left to call. No allies left to owe. Nobody coming to help. Just this room and whatever we built in it.
I don’t need you perfect tonight. I need you all the way in — every ounce you’ve got, right now, nothing saved back. There’s nothing to save it for.
Win or lose, this ends tomorrow. Let’s make sure nobody in this city ever forgets how we played it.
Decks are hot — let’s run it.

chapters.job: The finale. The crew becomes myth. A celebration of everything.
chapters.endsOn: The story closes. But legends never really end…
chapters.transmission:
Twenty-four nights. One crew. One impossible run.
They said it couldn’t be done. They said you’d turn on each other, get caught, get buried. Look around. You’re still standing.
What we built here doesn’t end when the lights come up. It becomes a story. The kind people tell for years. The kind that turns into legend.
You are the syndicate now. Every one of you.
Decks are hot — one last time. Let’s make it the loudest night this city has ever seen.

missions.name: THE LINEUP
missions.props: Height marker backdrop, single spotlight, phone with vertical camera ready
missions.howItRuns: Pull 3–5 people on stage. Line them up like a mugshot. Read each person’s mock “rap sheet” on mic (“Suspect #1: charged with looking too good tonight”). Take the photo. Crowd cheers loudest for the Most Wanted.
missions.win: Loudest crowd reaction = Most Wanted. Winner gets a drink ticket.
missions.handlerVO: Line ‘em up. Eyes forward. Don’t smile — you’re looking at a long sentence.

scene.cue: Music down to a low bed, not off. One spotlight on the height marker. You’re centre stage, mic in hand, clipboard or phone as the ‘file’.
scene.fourthWall:
Quick honesty break. This is a bar. You came out for a drink and some music, and nobody in this building has stolen anything heavier than a traffic cone.
And yet — for the next four minutes, every person in here has a record. I don’t make the rules. Actually, I do make the rules. That’s the entire point of me.

driver.actI: Every crew starts with a file. Before I put anybody on a job, I need to know what this city already has on you — so tonight we open the file and read it out loud.
driver.actII: There’s a detective building a photo book with our faces in it. If you’re going in it, I’d rather it be a good photo — and I’d rather we find out tonight who they can actually identify.
driver.actIII: The whole city’s got our description now. So let’s find out which one of you they’re really looking for — and which one of you they’d never suspect.

scene.rules:
Here’s how it works. Bodies against that wall — shoulder to shoulder, facing me, like you’ve done this before.
I read each of you your charges. You do not laugh, you do not smile, you hold the face.
Then this room decides which one of you is Most Wanted, and the loudest reaction takes it.
scene.callUp:
I need five. Don’t make me pick — but I will pick.
You. You. The one already walking up. And whoever’s friends are pointing at them right now. That’s how it always happens. Come on.
underscore: Suspect number three, chin up. This is the photo they’re going to use on the news.
Look at this lineup. Not one honest face in the row.
Somebody’s friend just yelled ‘that’s him.’ Noted. Recorded.
scene.win:
There it is. That’s the loudest this room has been all night, and it was for this one right here.
Congratulations — you are the most wanted person in this building. Enjoy the notoriety. It doesn’t last.
scene.out:
Get them out of my lineup. File’s open, the crew’s on record, and now we know exactly who this city is looking for.
Music back up.

missions.variation: MOST-WANTED RANKINGS — instead of one winner, the crowd ranks all 5 from “Most Wanted” to “Rookie.” Each rank gets a different mock charge.

missions.name: THE GETAWAY — BALLOON CHASE
missions.props: 20–30 red balloons (“getaway cars”), 20–30 blue balloons (“police”), tape boundaries on the floor
missions.howItRuns: Pull 5–6 people. Each gets ONE red balloon. The crowd gets the blue balloons. The crew has to keep their red balloon in the air for 60 seconds while the crowd bats blue balloons to knock theirs down. Last red balloon standing wins.
missions.win: Last crew member with their red balloon still in the air at the 60-second buzzer.
missions.handlerVO: Five stars. Choppers up. Keep your car in the air or you’re done.

scene.cue: Balloons pre-inflated and stashed behind the booth. Red ones out first, blue ones into the crowd on your cue. Tape boundary already down.
scene.fourthWall:
Time out. What’s about to happen is six adults protecting balloons from a room full of other adults. I want you to know that I know.
I’ve been doing this twenty-five years, and I’m telling you — this is the loudest three minutes of any night I run. So nobody be too cool for it.

driver.actI: Before I trust anybody with a getaway, I need to see how you move when something’s coming at you. Nobody’s chasing us yet. That’s what tonight is for.
driver.actII: There are cars on this block that weren’t here last week. This is the rehearsal — because when it’s real you get one shot at the road.
driver.actIII: This isn’t practice. Five stars, choppers up, a badge on every bridge. Show me you can get out.

scene.rules:
Red balloon is your car. Keep it in the air. That’s the whole job.
Everybody else gets a blue one — you are the police, and you have exactly one purpose: put their car on the ground. Bat it, spike it, be a menace about it.
Sixty seconds. Last car still in the air walks.
scene.callUp:
Six drivers. Hands up — real hands, up high.
You six, out in the middle, spread out. Everybody else: blue balloons are coming into the crowd, and I would like you to take this personally.
underscore: One star. Two. Three — dispatch just put out your description.
Blue team, you’re embarrassing yourselves. That car has been up for thirty seconds.
Down goes a car. Pour one out. Keep it moving.
scene.win:
One car still up. Everybody else is in the back of a van.
That’s your wheelman right there — the only one who made it out.
scene.out:
Balloons on the floor, leave them, we’ll deal with it. Crew got out clean tonight and that’s all I needed to know.
Back to the music.

missions.variation: ESCALATION MODE — every 20 seconds you call up the wanted level and add more blue balloons. By 60s the room is chaos.

missions.name: THE SHOOTOUT — NERF GALLERY
missions.props: 2–3 Nerf guns (dart blasters), 5–6 cardboard target cutouts (silhouettes painted black & pink), a folding table
missions.howItRuns: Pull 3 contestants. Each gets 10 darts. 30 seconds to knock down as many targets as possible. Crowd counts down. Highest score wins.
missions.win: Most targets knocked down in 30 seconds.
missions.handlerVO: This is what we trained you for. Don’t miss.

scene.cue: Targets on the table, blasters loaded and laid out, darts counted to ten per shooter. Keep the firing line pointed away from the bar.
scene.fourthWall:
Nobody’s getting hurt tonight. That’s foam, those are cardboard, and my insurance is very clear on the subject.
But I need you to react like it’s real — because a room that plays along is worth more to me than a room that’s honest.

driver.actI: Everybody in a crew says they can handle themselves. Tonight I find out who actually can, while it’s still free to find out.
driver.actII: The dry run happens in here, where mistakes cost nothing. Miss in this room and we laugh. Miss in that vault and we don’t.
driver.actIII: It went loud out there. So here’s what I need answered tonight: when it goes loud, whose hands stay steady?

scene.rules:
Ten darts each. Thirty seconds. Every target you put down counts.
You do not pick darts up, you do not get a reload. Ten shots is what this crew could afford.
Most targets down takes it.
scene.callUp:
Three shooters. I want the ones who look too confident — you, you, and whoever just said ‘I got this’ loud enough for me to hear it.
Up here.
underscore: Twenty seconds, four darts left. The math is not on your side.
That’s the worst shot I’ve seen in twenty-five years. Do it again.
This room counts out loud or it doesn’t count at all.
scene.win:
That’s the crew’s best shot right there.
Remember this face — when it goes sideways, this is who I’m putting at the front.
scene.out:
Darts stay where they are, we’ll get them. Crew can handle itself — that was the last thing I needed to know.
Music up.

missions.variation: MOVING TARGETS — a staffer walks behind the table holding targets above their head (safely above shoulders), making them moving. Bigger laughs, more skill required.

missions.name: THE DEAD DROP — BRIEFCASE HOT POTATO
missions.props: 1 black briefcase ($15 on Amazon), filler weight inside, silly reward (candy, fake cash, stickers)
missions.howItRuns: Earlier in the night, hand the briefcase to someone in the crowd: “Keep it moving. Don’t open it. If you’re holding it when the music stops, you’re holding the evidence.” The briefcase circulates while you DJ. At mission time, cut the music abruptly. Whoever’s holding it comes to stage. They open it OR pick a silly punishment.
missions.win: Be holding it when the music stops. Or don’t. Either way the bit pays off.
missions.time: 2 min on stage (background play happens during 30+ min of the set)
missions.handlerVO: Drop’s active. Don’t look at the briefcase. Don’t talk about the briefcase. Move it.

scene.cue: The handoff line goes out 30+ minutes before the payoff, quietly, to one person mid-set. The rest of this scene runs the moment you cut the music.
scene.fourthWall:
Somewhere in this room, for the last half hour, a black briefcase has been quietly ruining somebody’s night.
And every single one of you who touched it made the same face — the ‘am I actually in trouble’ face. That face is why I do this job.

driver.actI: A crew that can’t move product can’t move anything. That case went hand to hand all night and nobody dropped it — you passed a test you didn’t know you were taking.
driver.actII: Everything we need moves through hands like yours. There are eyes on this room, so the case never stops and never opens. Tonight we find out where it ended up.
driver.actIII: The take is still moving through this room. Whoever’s holding it right now is holding the evidence — and the music is about to stop.

scene.rules:
[Handoff, delivered early and quiet:] Take this. Don’t open it, don’t set it down, don’t ask what’s in it. Keep it moving and keep your mouth shut.
One thing, though — if you’re holding it when the music stops, you’re holding the evidence. And I will find you.
scene.callUp:
Music’s off. Nobody move.
Whoever has the case — and this room knows exactly who has the case — bring it to me. Take your time. Everybody’s watching.
underscore: Don’t look at the briefcase. Don’t talk about the briefcase. Move the briefcase.
Somebody just handed that off like it was on fire. Coward. Respect.
That case has been in this room thirty minutes and nobody’s opened it. Disciplined crew.
scene.win:
Two options. Open it — right here, in front of everybody — or take the punishment and let it stay a mystery.
Room’s going to help you decide.
scene.out:
Case is closed. Whatever was in it, we never discussed it.
Everybody back to what you were doing. Music.

missions.variation: TIMED DROPS — cut the music 2–3 times across the night instead of once. Each “drop” gets a smaller bit; the final drop is the big stage moment.

missions.name: THE INFORMANT HUNT — FIND THE RAT
missions.props: 5 colored wristbands handed out at the door (4 the same color, 1 different)
missions.howItRuns: At doors, secretly hand 5 people wristbands — four matching, one odd. At mission time: “Crew check. If you got a wristband, to the stage.” On stage, the crowd has to spot which one is the rat (the odd-colored band). Once identified, the rat does a punishment moment. The four crew get small rewards.
missions.win: Crowd correctly identifies the rat by band color.
missions.handlerVO: Somebody in this crew’s wearing a wire. Find them before the score goes down.

scene.cue: Bands go out at the door, quietly, to five people — four matching, one odd. Note who has the odd one so you can call it if the room can’t.
scene.fourthWall:
Let me admit something. Nobody in here is a rat. You’re all lovely. Half of you are here for somebody’s birthday.
But for the next three minutes this room is going to turn on one person over the colour of a bracelet, and you’re going to enjoy it more than you expect.

driver.actI: Somebody in this crew is already working two sides. I told you that on night two — I wasn’t guessing.
driver.actII: The cops got a name, and names come from people. One of the five standing up here handed it over.
driver.actIII: The count came up short and somebody made a phone call. Tonight we find out who’s been talking.

scene.rules:
Five of you got a band at the door tonight. Four of them match. One doesn’t.
The one that doesn’t match is the rat — and this room has to work out which. No confessions, no help from me.
Look at the wrists. Listen to the room. Make the call.
scene.callUp:
Crew check. If you got a band at the door, that’s you — to the stage.
All five. Yes, you too. Don’t play.
underscore: Somebody in this crew is wearing a wire. Find them before the score goes down.
Look at the hands. A rat always covers the wrist.
This room is far too good at this. Genuinely concerning.
scene.win:
There’s your rat. Caught by their own bracelet.
The four of you are clean, you’re crew, you get looked after. And you — you’ve got some explaining to do.
scene.out:
Rat’s handled, crew’s clean again. For now.
Nobody in this room says a word about how easy that was. Music up.

missions.variation: DOUBLE RAT — hand out 6 wristbands (4 matching, 2 odd). Crowd has to find BOTH rats. Higher difficulty, bigger payoff.

missions.name: THE BAGMAN — BEACH BALL VAULT FILL
missions.gtaRef: Looting the vault / stuffing the duffel
missions.props: 4–5 beach balls (spray-painted gold = “money bags”), 2 large bins / laundry baskets / boxes
missions.howItRuns: Two teams of 3 pulled from the crowd. Beach balls are tossed into the crowd at the start. Teams have to retrieve as many “money bags” from the crowd and get them into THEIR team’s bin within 60 seconds. The crowd is the obstacle — they can throw them, hide them, bat them away.
missions.win: Most balls in your team’s bin at the 60-second buzzer.
missions.handlerVO: Vault’s open. Grab everything you can. Don’t leave a dollar.

scene.cue: Beach balls into the crowd at the top of the scene, not before — they disappear fast. Bins set well apart so the two teams have to cross the room.
scene.fourthWall:
I’d like to state plainly that those are beach balls painted gold, and those are laundry baskets.
And in about ten seconds you’re going to care about them more than anything that’s happened to you this week. That’s not me being clever — that’s just what a room does.

driver.actI: You’ll never touch the big score if you can’t handle a small take. Tonight’s take is small.
driver.actII: When that vault opens we get sixty seconds inside it. Sixty. So let’s find out what this crew can carry in sixty seconds.
driver.actIII: Vault’s open, the take is real, the clock is running. Grab everything you can and don’t leave a dollar.

scene.rules:
Two crews of three. That’s your bin. That’s yours.
The money’s already out in the crowd, and the crowd is not on your side — they can throw it, hide it, sit on it, send it back.
Sixty seconds. Most money in your bin wins.
scene.callUp:
Two crews, three each. I want people who don’t mind getting into a crowd.
You three on that bin, you three on that one. Everybody else — the money’s coming to you, and you should be a problem about it.
underscore: Vault’s open. Grab everything you can. Don’t leave a dollar.
Somebody in the crowd is just holding one. Sir. That is not yours.
Fifteen seconds and that bin is embarrassing.
scene.win:
Count it. That’s the take, and this crew carried it.
Winners get looked after. Losers can explain the shortfall to the people upstairs.
scene.out:
Money’s in the bin, crowd keeps whatever’s left, we’re gone. Vault’s empty.
Let’s move. Music.

missions.variation: GUARD MODE — one player from each team is designated “guard” — they stand at their bin and can deflect incoming balls from the other team. Adds defense to offense.

missions.name: THE HACK — LASER GRID
missions.props: 2 A-frame stands or chair posts, 3–4 rolls of red crepe streamer OR red string + masking tape, blacklight optional
missions.howItRuns: Set up a “laser grid” between two stands at the front of the stage — a web of crisscrossed red lines across a 6-foot doorway. Pull 2–3 contestants. They have to crawl, duck, or limbo through without touching a single line. Crowd counts touches.
missions.win: Fewest lines touched. Fastest time as tiebreaker.
missions.handlerVO: One wrong move and the whole place lights up. Take your time. Don’t. Touch. Anything.

scene.cue: Grid built before doors if you can — it takes longer than you think. Blacklight on it if you’ve got one. Keep a spare roll of streamer for repairs mid-scene.
scene.fourthWall:
That is crepe paper. It’s a dollar a roll. There’s no laser, there’s no alarm, and if you touch it the only thing that happens is this room makes a noise.
Somehow that’s worse. That’s exactly why it works.

driver.actI: Every door on this job is electric. Before I bring in the tech, I want to see who in here has the patience for it.
driver.actII: That system belongs to the biggest boss in this city and it does not care how tough you are. One wrong move and the whole place lights up.
driver.actIII: We’re past the alarms and into the part where one twitch ends it for everybody. Slow is smooth. Smooth is out.

scene.rules:
This is the grid, and every line on it is live.
You get through — over, under, through, I don’t care how — without touching a single one. This room counts every touch out loud, and the count follows you for the rest of the night.
Fewest touches takes it. Fastest breaks a tie.
scene.callUp:
Give me two — and I want one person who’s flexible and one who absolutely is not.
That contrast is the whole show. Up here.
underscore: Take your time. Don’t. Touch. Anything.
That’s one. The whole room heard it. The building heard it.
Look at this — genuine technique. Somebody’s done this before.
scene.win:
Clean run. That’s our way in.
Everybody else here would have had the whole block surrounded.
scene.out:
Grid’s down, system’s ours, nobody set off an alarm. That’s how this is supposed to go.
Music back.

missions.variation: BLINDFOLD HACK — same grid, but contestant is blindfolded and their partner from the crowd has to talk them through it using only voice. Doubled comedy.

missions.name: THE BLUEPRINT — MEMORY GRID
missions.props: A board, posterboard, or projection showing 12–16 simple icons (guns, cars, dollar signs, masks, badges) in a grid
missions.howItRuns: Show the grid for 10 seconds. Cover it. Pull 3 contestants. Each gets 30 seconds (separately) to recall as many icons as possible. Most correct recalls wins.
missions.handlerVO: Memorize it. You only get one look. Get this wrong and the whole job’s blown.

scene.cue: Board covered before anybody’s looking. Have a timer you can actually see — ten seconds by feel is always wrong. Keep the room quiet for this one; it’s the only game that needs it.
scene.fourthWall:
This is the one nobody volunteers for, because this one’s actually hard.
No hiding behind being loud here. It’s just you and whether you’ve been paying attention — which, let’s be honest, most of us have not been tonight.

driver.actI: Before I hand out roles I need to know who in here can hold a plan in their head.
driver.actII: We’re casing the target. You get one look at the layout and you get it tonight — because on the night there is no second look.
driver.actIII: Everything from here runs on memory. Nothing written down, nothing on a phone. What you remember is all we’ve got.

scene.rules:
Ten seconds. That’s your one look at the layout — every icon on that board.
Then it’s covered, and one at a time you tell me everything you can remember. Thirty seconds each, no help from the room.
Most correct takes it.
scene.callUp: Three of you. I want the one who says they’ve got a great memory — you’re going first, and I want this room to hold you to it.
underscore: Memorize it. You only get one look. Get this wrong and the whole job’s blown.
Room — not a word. Don’t you dare help them.
Ten seconds doesn’t sound like much until you’re the one standing here.
scene.win:
That’s the best head in the building.
You’re on the blueprint. Everybody else is carrying something heavy.
scene.out:
Layout’s locked. This crew knows the room now — whether they remember it or not.
Music up.

missions.variation: GROUP RECALL — instead of solo, three contestants take turns naming icons round-robin without repeats. First to repeat or blank is out. Last standing wins.

missions.name: THE CAR JACK — KEYS IN THE BUCKET
missions.props: 1 bucket, ~30 fake car keys (cheap dollar-store sets or printed cutouts), one labeled “GETAWAY KEY” in bold
missions.howItRuns: Pass the bucket of keys into the crowd earlier in the night — each person grabs ONE without looking. At mission time: “We need a wheelman. Whoever’s got the GETAWAY KEY — to the stage.” Whoever finds it wins. If nobody steps up in 60 seconds, you reveal who actually has it.
missions.handlerVO: One of you walked out of here with the keys to the score. Find them. Bring them to me.

scene.cue: Bucket goes through the room early, one key each, nobody looks. Know who took the marked key so you can name them if nobody comes up.
scene.fourthWall:
Half of you took a key out of a bucket earlier tonight without asking a single question about why.
I want you to sit with that. A stranger handed you a bucket and you just took one. This is how it starts.

driver.actI: A score like ours lives or dies on ninety seconds of road, and we still don’t have a driver. One of you has been carrying the keys all night.
driver.actII: Two ways in, one way out — and the way out needs a car. Whoever’s holding the getaway key is holding the whole plan.
driver.actIII: Every bridge is watched and there’s one car that can still get us out of this city. One of you has the key to it. Find it. Now.

scene.rules:
A bucket of keys went through this room and exactly one of them is marked.
If you’re holding the getaway key, you’re our wheelman — bring it up.
Sixty seconds. After that I name whoever’s got it, whether they come up or not.
scene.callUp:
One of you walked out of here with the keys to the score.
Find them. Bring them to me. Clock’s on.
underscore: Somebody in here is holding it and still hasn’t looked. Classic.
Check your pocket. Check your friend’s pocket. Check the floor.
Thirty seconds and no wheelman. This is how crews die.
scene.win:
That’s the key. That’s our driver.
Everybody get a look at the person who’s about to get us out of here.
scene.out:
We’ve got a car and we’ve got a driver. Keys stay with them.
Everybody else — yours were always fake. Sorry about that. Music.

missions.variation: MULTIPLE KEYS — mark 3 keys (gold, silver, bronze) with different rewards. Three winners, three tiers of prize.

missions.name: THE TAKEDOWN — TUG OF WAR
missions.gtaRef: Crew vs rival crew turf war
missions.props: One rope (10–15 ft, soft cotton/poly so nobody gets burned), tape line on the floor for the center
missions.howItRuns: Pull two teams of 3 from the crowd. Mark a center line on the floor. Quick 30-second tug of war — first team pulled across loses. Losers do a silly punishment (lead a chant, take a group photo as the “arrested crew”). Winners get drink tickets each.
missions.win: Pull the other team across the center line, OR have more team on your side at the 30-second buzzer.
missions.handlerVO: Two crews. One city. Only one of you walks out tonight — the other one goes down.

scene.cue: Centre line taped before doors. Check the rope for grit, clear a body-length behind each team, and make sure nobody’s holding a drink.
scene.fourthWall:
Two teams, one rope. This is the oldest game there is and I have never once seen a room not lose its mind for it.
No story I could write beats what’s about to happen naturally, so I’m getting out of the way after this sentence.

driver.actI: Another crew’s been sniffing around what’s ours. Tonight we find out whether this room can hold a line.
driver.actII: The rival crew wants their hardware back and they’re not asking nicely. Two crews, one city.
driver.actIII: Everybody who came at this crew answers tonight. Only one side walks out of this.

scene.rules:
Three on each end. Feet behind the line — that line, the one on the floor.
Thirty seconds. Pull the other crew across and it’s done. Nobody goes over, whoever’s got more ground when I call it takes it.
And losers don’t walk away quietly. Losers get arrested.
scene.callUp:
Two crews of three. Pick your own — that’s half the entertainment, and I want to see who nobody picks.
Rope in the middle. Don’t touch it yet.
underscore: Two crews. One city. Only one of you walks out tonight.
This room is nowhere near loud enough for what’s happening on this rope.
Ten seconds. Somebody’s about to find out who their friends are.
scene.win:
That’s the crew that holds this block.
The other three — you’re getting arrested, and this room is taking the photo.
scene.out:
Turf’s settled, rope’s down, nobody needed stitches. Good night’s work.
Music back up.

missions.variation: BEST OF THREE — instead of one pull, run three quick rounds. Winners switch sides each round. Best record takes it.

missions.name: THE STAKEOUT — CUP STACK SPEED
missions.props: 12 red Solo cups per contestant ($5 on Amazon for plenty), folding table
missions.howItRuns: Pull 3 contestants. Each gets 12 cups in a stack. Race: build a pyramid (6-3-2-1 or 3-2-1 stacked twice = 12 cups), knock it clean, then re-stack into the starting column. First to finish wins. Crowd counts down from 60.
missions.win: First to complete the full sequence (pyramid up, knocked down, re-stacked to single column).
missions.handlerVO: Set the rig. Sixty seconds. We move when you’re ready.

scene.cue: Twelve cups per shooter, pre-counted and stacked. Table steady — a wobbly table ruins this one. Room counts down from sixty out loud.
scene.fourthWall:
Twelve plastic cups. That’s the entire prop budget for this one.
And I promise the last thirty seconds of this will be louder than anything else in this room tonight, because nothing makes people scream like watching somebody almost drop something.

driver.actI: Before the job comes the prep, and the prep is boring, and boring is where crews fall apart. Let’s see who’s got the hands.
driver.actII: We build the rig tonight. Set it, break it down, set it again — because on the night we’re doing this in the dark with somebody watching the door.
driver.actIII: One job left, and it starts with the rig. Sixty seconds to build, break, and be gone. Nothing left behind.

scene.rules:
Twelve cups each. Build the pyramid, knock it flat, stack it back into one column. All three, in that order.
Knock it early and it doesn’t count. Rush the restack and you’ll be picking cups off the floor.
First one done takes it — and this room counts down from sixty.
scene.callUp:
Three of you at the table. Steady hands only.
And if you’ve got long nails I want you up here specifically, because I want to watch.
underscore: Set the rig. Sixty seconds. We move when you’re ready.
That pyramid is a war crime. Fix it.
Twenty seconds. One of these three is about to panic and I want to be there for it.
scene.win:
Rig built, broken down and packed in under a minute.
That’s the steadiest set of hands in the building.
scene.out:
Prep’s done. Everything we need is ready and nothing’s left on the table.
Now the only thing between us and the score is time. Music.

missions.variation: TEAM RELAY — two teams of 3, relay-style. First person stacks the pyramid, second knocks it down, third re-stacks. Faster, louder, team energy.
